claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has a coercive field of approximately 100 Oe.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization.
Moderate-temperature aging can induce ordering or nanoscale precipitation in an initially homogeneous alloy.
Aging fcc FeCoNi at approximately 500 °C for 4 hours will produce short-range ordered regions or fine coherent nanoprecipitates within its fcc matrix.
The induced ordered regions or coherent nanoprecipitates will act as domain-wall pinning centers.
Additional domain-wall pinning will impede domain-wall motion and increase coercivity.
The aging treatment will increase coercivity beyond 100 Oe, ideally to approximately 200 Oe or more.
The aging-induced coercivity increase can be achieved while limiting saturation-magnetization loss to less than 10%.
Solution annealing ensures a homogeneous starting microstructure in FeCoNi or a closely related derivative.
The effective processing window is 450–550 °C for durations of a few hours.
Substantial deviations from the proposed aging window may cause unwanted phase transformations or degradation of magnetization.
Prior work suggests that annealing conditions can alter ordering or decomposition in related high-entropy alloys.
Prior work supports beneficial short-range ordering as the source of enhanced coercivity in alloys similar to fcc FeCoNi.
XRD and TEM characterization can establish whether the proposed short-range ordering or coherent nanoprecipitates formed.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome describes approximately 200 Oe as an ideal target, implying that a smaller but significant increase above 100 Oe could support the hypothesis, whereas the falsification rule treats any result below approximately 200 Oe as falsifying it.
